[LERR.9.7] **When the fact is asserted.** A fault is raised part-way through
something — a `TypeError` during matching, in the middle of propagating another
fact; a fault in an activation, part-way through its actions. The engine
**must not** assert a fault fact at that point. It **must** queue fault facts in
the order the faults are recorded ([LERR.1.4.12] orders those raised while
matching) and assert them when the current propagation has
completed, or when the abandoned activation has been unwound, and in any case
before the next agenda selection. Each takes its timetag when asserted, like any
fact, and a handler's activation is ordered by [LDET.5] with no special case.

**At most one fault is pending per `(node, rule)` site between a raise and the
drain.** A later fault at a site whose fault is still pending replaces it in
place: the site keeps the queue position of its first pending fault. The
stream carries the drained facts only, so the intermediate ones never
appear. The queue is thereby bounded by the site count ([LERR.9.10]) in every
mode: a pre-sized runtime holds it without growing, and a runtime that is not
pre-sized records the same stream.
